excerpt: Squire is booking, payments and shop-management software built for barbershops, with a client app for booking barbers. Founded in New York in 2016; valued at $750M in 2021.
content:
Squire makes software for barbershops. Its shop app, SQUIRE Commander, describes an all-in-one platform for running a barbershop: appointment scheduling and online booking (including booking from Instagram), point of sale with Apple Pay and card readers, product and service sales, inventory, payroll, gift cards and loyalty, a waitlist, barber bios and marketing texts and emails to clients. Its customer app, SQUIRE, lets people find barbers near them, check availability, book a time and pay for the cut and tip with a card on file.

Squire was launched in 2016 in New York by Songe LaRon and Dave Salvant, according to TechCrunch; Forbes described the pair as a former corporate lawyer and a finance professional who left those careers to build the company. TechCrunch reported in June 2020 that Squire had raised a $34 million Series B led by CRV just before barbershops were shut down by the pandemic, after an $8 million Series A led by Trinity Ventures. When shops closed, Squire waived subscription fees and helped barbers sell gift cards online.

As shops reopened, demand for digital booking and payments grew. In July 2021 Fortune reported that Squire raised $60 million in a Series D that tripled its valuation to $750 million; the round was led by Tiger Global. Fortune noted that Squire's revenues had plummeted at the start of stay-at-home orders before recovering as barbershops went digital.

Squire's website could not be loaded for this profile, so we could not check its current plans or prices on the official pricing page and do not quote any. Ask Squire for a demo or quote. This profile draws on published reporting and Squire's App Store listings. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
